reference.title: Sentinel and regional node criteria
reference.intro: For reference while choosing; nothing here prints.

groups.heading: Breast: the largest deposit
points: Micrometastasis: more than 0.2 mm and up to 2 mm, or more than 200 cells in a single cross-section; pN1mi when none is larger.
Isolated tumour cells: single cells or clusters 0.2 mm or less, or fewer than 200 cells in a single cross-section, on H&E or immunohistochemistry; pN0(i+), counted as examined but not as positive.
Measure the largest group of touching tumour cells, including any part outside the node or in an adjacent lymphatic; the distance between clusters is not added.

More than 200 dispersed or nearly confluent cells in one section of a node is a micrometastasis (about 1000 cells fill a 0.2 mm cluster). The 200 cells must lie in a single node profile; cells in different sections or levels are not added. The threshold is a guide: judge whether the cluster is a true micrometastasis.

groups.heading: Extranodal extension
points: Tumour extending through the lymph node capsule into the adjacent tissue.
Extent beyond the capsule: 2 mm or less, or more than 2 mm; measured perpendicular to the capsule or in another dimension, the larger measurement preferred.
The part outside the node is included in the size of the deposit.

groups.heading: Breast: after presurgical therapy
points: ypN uses the largest contiguous focus of residual tumour; treatment-related fibrosis beside it is not measured.

Treatment effect in the nodes: no definite response in metastatic carcinoma; metastatic carcinoma with response (for example small deposits within fibrosis); no metastasis but fibrous scarring or histiocytic aggregates, possibly a prior metastasis with complete response; no metastasis and no scarring or aggregates.

groups.heading: Melanoma
points: Any metastatic tumour cells, however few, on H&E or immunohistochemistry make the node positive; there is no isolated tumour cell category.
Record the largest discrete deposit (cells in direct continuity) to the nearest 0.1 mm: the largest single deposit, not the area the deposits are scattered over.
Location: subcapsular sinus, nodal parenchyma, or both.
Nodal naevus: bland cells in the capsule and trabeculae, no mitoses, minimal HMB45 and Ki-67 below 2%; isolated Melan-A-positive cells are not overinterpreted.

reference.note: Breast: AJCC 8th edition as given in the CAP breast protocol 4.11 (June 2026) and the QMH template. Melanoma: AJCC 8th edition, the ICCR melanoma dataset and the CAP melanoma protocol.
